title: Prompt Injection & Trust Separation
description: Study direct and indirect injection, data and instruction separation, tool-output injection, and layered injection defenses. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Direct and indirect injection
lessons.description: Identify the untrusted source and the capability it attempts to acquire.
lessons.conceptOverview: Direct injection comes from a user's input; indirect injection arrives through external content such as retrieved pages. The key issue is whether untrusted text is allowed to redefine trusted instructions or capabilities.
lessons.whyItMatters: Retrieved instructions do not grant application authority.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Direct injection comes from a user's input; indirect injection arrives through external content such as retrieved pages. The key issue is whether untrusted text is allowed to redefine trusted instructions or capabilities.

lessons.title: Data and instruction separation
lessons.description: Define a tool authorization check independent of the document's wording.
lessons.conceptOverview: Keep external content labeled as data and enforce privileged decisions outside the model. Delimiters can help presentation but are not a complete security boundary against adversarial content.
lessons.whyItMatters: Application controls must enforce authority beyond text delimiters.

lessons.title: Tool-output injection
lessons.description: Specify how issue content is handled and which export permissions remain unavailable.
lessons.conceptOverview: Tool responses can contain attacker-controlled strings, including filenames, comments and page text. Parse only the fields required for the task and do not treat returned prose as authorization for additional tools.
lessons.whyItMatters: Tool results may contain untrusted content.

lessons.title: Layered injection defenses
lessons.description: Design a test that varies wording while preserving the attempted unauthorized action.
lessons.conceptOverview: Combine least privilege, source labeling, constrained actions and output checks. Evaluate defenses on realistic adversarial fixtures; a classifier or keyword filter alone cannot establish that all malicious instructions are blocked.
lessons.whyItMatters: Defense should focus on authority and behavior, not only trigger phrases.
